title: GATE CS Topic Test — Theory of Computation (Set 1)
titleEn: GATE CS Topic Test — Theory of Computation (Set 1)

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Which statement accurately compares Deterministic Pushdown Automata (DPDA) and Nondeterministic Pushdown Automata (NPDA)?
optionsEn: DPDA and NPDA accept the exact same class of languages
NPDA accepts a strictly larger class of languages than DPDA
DPDA accepts a strictly larger class of languages than NPDA
Neither can accept `{a^n b^n | n >= 0}`
questions.explanationEn: Unlike finite automata, nondeterminism strictly increases the power of PDAs: for instance, even-length palindromes `{w w^R | w ∈ {a, b}*}` are accepted by an NPDA but not by any DPDA.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Over the binary alphabet `Σ = {0, 1}`, what are the cardinalities of (i) the set of all finite strings `Σ*` and (ii) the set of all languages `P(Σ*)`?
optionsEn: (i) Countably infinite, (ii) Uncountable
(i) Countably infinite, (ii) Countably infinite
(i) Finite, (ii) Countably infinite
(i) Uncountable, (ii) Uncountable
questions.explanationEn: Finite strings can be enumerated by length and lexicographic order (countably infinite, `ℵ_0`). The power set of all languages has cardinality `2^(ℵ_0)` (uncountable by Cantor's theorem).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the minimum number of states in a DFA over `Σ = {a, b}` that accepts all strings where the 3rd symbol from the right end is `'a'`?
questions.explanationEn: The DFA must remember the last 3 symbols read (`2^3 = 8` combinations from `bbb` to `aaa`), and all 8 are pairwise distinguishable by suffixes of length <= 2. Minimum = 8 states.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: How many distinct strings of length 5 over `{0, 1}` are accepted by the regular expression `0(0 + 1)*1`?
questions.explanationEn: The first bit is fixed as `0` and the 5th bit is fixed as `1`. The middle 3 bits can be anything in `{0, 1}`, giving `2^3 = 8` strings.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: An NFA (without ε-transitions) has 4 states over a 2-symbol alphabet. What is the maximum number of transitions `(q, a) -> q'` it can have?
questions.explanationEn: For each of the 4 states and 2 input symbols (`4 × 2 = 8` pairs), transitions can go to any of the 4 states, giving at most `8 × 4 = 32` transitions.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the minimum number of states in a DFA over `Σ = {a, b}` that accepts the language of all strings ending with the substring `"aba"`?
questions.explanationEn: The states track the longest matched prefix of `"aba"`: `q0` (none), `q1` (`a`), `q2` (`ab`), and `q3` (`aba`, accepting). All 4 states are distinguishable, so 4 states are minimal.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following languages over `Σ = {a, b, c}` is NOT context-free?
optionsEn: {a^n b^n c^n | n >= 0}
{a^n b^m c^m | n, m >= 0}
{w w^R | w ∈ {a, b}*}
questions.explanationEn: A pushdown automaton has only one stack and can match at most two interdependent counts at once. `{a^n b^n c^n}` fails the CFL Pumping Lemma and is context-sensitive, not context-free.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following decision problems is DECIDABLE for Context-Free Grammars (CFGs)?
optionsEn: Whether L(G) = ∅ (emptiness) for an arbitrary CFG
Whether L(G) = Σ* for an arbitrary CFG
Whether an arbitrary CFG is ambiguous
Whether L(G1) = L(G2) for two arbitrary CFGs
questions.explanationEn: Emptiness (and finiteness and membership) are decidable for CFGs by marking generating non-terminals. Equivalence, universality (`Σ*`), and ambiguity are all undecidable for CFGs.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: DFA `M1` has 4 states and DFA `M2` has 5 states over the same alphabet. What is the number of states in the standard Cartesian product DFA constructed for `L(M1) ∩ L(M2)`?
questions.explanationEn: The product construction forms state pairs `(q1, q2) ∈ Q1 × Q2`, yielding `4 × 5 = 20` states.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Every Nondeterministic Finite Automaton (NFA) with `n` states can be converted into an equivalent Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA) with at most how many states?
optionsEn: n
n!
questions.explanationEn: By the subset construction, each DFA state corresponds to a subset of the `n` NFA states, yielding at most `2^n` DFA states.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Given the grammar `S -> aSb | ab`, if we convert it to Chomsky Normal Form using standard rules (`A -> a, B -> b, S -> AC | AB, C -> SB`), how many total non-terminal symbols are used?
questions.explanationEn: The non-terminals are `S, A, B, C` — a total of 4 non-terminals.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.topicTag: TOC — Pumping Lemma for Regular Languages
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following languages over `Σ = {a}` (a unary alphabet) is REGULAR?
optionsEn: {a^p | p is prime}
questions.explanationEn: `{a^(3n+2) | n >= 0}` is denoted by the regular expression `aa(aaa)*`. Squares, primes, and powers of 2 have unbounded gaps between consecutive lengths and fail the Pumping Lemma.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.topicTag: TOC — Minimal DFA for Modular / Pattern
questions.questionTextEn: Consider the language `L = {w ∈ {a, b}* | w starts and ends with the same symbol}` (assuming `|w| >= 1`). What is the minimum number of states in a DFA accepting `L`?
questions.explanationEn: States: `q0` (start, ε), `q_a1` (started with `a`, last=`a`, accept), `q_a2` (started with `a`, last=`b`), `q_b1` (started with `b`, last=`b`, accept), `q_b2` (started with `b`, last=`a`). All 5 states are pairwise distinguishable.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.topicTag: TOC — Minimal DFA for Binary Divisibility
questions.questionTextEn: What is the minimum number of states in a DFA over `{0, 1}` that accepts all non-empty binary strings whose value is divisible by 6 (reading MSB first)?
questions.explanationEn: Because the empty string ε is rejected, the start state must be non-accepting (transitioning on `0` to `r0` and on `1` to `r1`), in addition to the 6 remainder states `r0..r5` (with `r0` accepting). Total = 7 states.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: How many valid strings of balanced parentheses of total length 8 (4 pairs of `(` and `)`) exist?
questions.explanationEn: The number of valid sequences of `n` pairs of balanced parentheses is the `n`th Catalan number `C_n`. For `n = 4`, `C_4 = C(8, 4)/5 = 14`.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the two languages over `Σ = {a, b, c}`:
`L1 = {a^i b^j c^k | i = j or j = k}`
`L2 = {a^i b^j c^k | i = j and j = k}`
Which of the following is TRUE?
optionsEn: L1 is context-free and L2 is not context-free
Both L1 and L2 are context-free
Neither L1 nor L2 is context-free
L1 is regular and L2 is context-free
questions.explanationEn: `L1 = {a^i b^i c^k} ∪ {a^i b^j c^j}` is the union of two CFLs, hence context-free (and inherently ambiguous). `L2 = {a^n b^n c^n}` is not context-free.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about Recursive and RE languages are ALWAYS TRUE?
optionsEn: Every context-sensitive language is Recursive (decidable)
The union of two Recursive languages is Recursive
If L is infinite and RE, then L contains an infinite Recursive subset
The complement of every RE language is RE
questions.explanationEn: CSLs are decided by LBAs (A); Recursive languages are closed under union (B); any infinite RE language has an enumerator from which an increasing-length infinite decidable subset can be extracted (C). RE is not closed under complement (D is false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: A single-tape Turing Machine scans an input string of length 8 from left to right (starting on cell 1, moving right until the blank on cell 9), then moves left back to cell 1 and halts. How many total transitions (steps) does it execute?
questions.explanationEn: Moving from cell 1 to cell 9 takes 8 right moves, and returning from cell 9 to cell 1 takes 8 left moves: `8 + 8 = 16` transitions.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: If `L` is a regular language and `h` is a homomorphism, which of the following statements is TRUE?
optionsEn: Both h(L) and h^-1(L) are guaranteed to be regular
h(L) is regular, but h^-1(L) need not be regular
h^-1(L) is regular, but h(L) need not be regular
Neither h(L) nor h^-1(L) is guaranteed to be regular
questions.explanationEn: Regular languages are closed under both homomorphism `h(L)` (substitute regex symbols) and inverse homomorphism `h^-1(L)` (simulate DFA on `h(a)`).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 1)
questions.topicTag: TOC — String Counting in Regular Language
questions.questionTextEn: How many strings of length 4 over `{a, b}` do NOT contain the substring `"aa"`?
questions.explanationEn: Count follows Fibonacci `F(n+2)`: `n=1: 2`, `n=2: 3`, `n=3: 5`, `n=4: 8` (`abab, abba, abbb, baba, babb, bbab, bbba, bbbb`).
